p0.original: 关键问题：意识与其他心理过程有何联系
p0.en: Key issue: How awareness relates to other psychological processes

p2.original: 大脑同时在意识和无意识的多个水平上运作。
p2.en: The brain operates at multiple levels, both conscious and unconscious.

p3.original: 有意识意味着什么？是警觉吗？还是指对自己和环境的觉知呢？这两种观点都看似合理。但请考虑一下这种情况：生理学家奥托·勒维（Otto Loewi）在睡梦中发现了神经元之间的化学传递（而非之前认为的电传递），之后他从梦中醒来，在床边的纸上潦草地写下了他的想法。他回去接着睡觉，但第二天早晨他却发现辨认不出自己的笔迹，也记不起自己梦中的实验设计。幸运的是，第二天晚上他做了同样的梦，而这一次他立即起床并冲进了实验室，进行了这个实验——这为他在1936年因对医学的贡献而获得诺贝尔奖奠定了基础。
p3.en: What does consciousness mean? Is it alert? What about your perception of yourself and your environment? Both views seem reasonable. But consider the situation: Otto Loewi, the physiologist, discovered the chemical transfer of neurons in his sleep (rather than the electricity that he had previously thought) and then woke up from his dream and wrote his thoughts on the bedside paper. He went back to sleep, but the next morning he found no identification of his handwriting, nor did he remember the design of the experiment in his dream. Fortunately, he had the same dream the next night, and this time he immediately got up and rushed into the laboratory, carrying out the experiment, which laid the foundation for his Nobel Prize for his contribution to medicine in 1936.

p4.original: 那么问题来了：当勒维在睡梦中设计出这一突破性的实验时，他是否是有意识的？虽然我们通常认为，警觉是思维清晰或问题解决（例如，勒维在睡梦中产生想法）的先决条件，但我们通常不认为睡觉或做梦是一种警觉状态，所以我们可能不会说他当时是警觉的。由于第二天早晨他发现无法读懂自己所写的内容，那么当他写下自己的想法时，他是有意识的吗？他有足够的意识去拿笔和纸，而我们通常认为，人必须有意识才能完成这种目标导向的行为。但是，如果他在写下想法的时候是有意识的，那么为什么他在第二天却无法理解自己所写的内容呢？
p4.en: So the question is: Was Levi conscious when he designed this breakthrough experiment in his sleep? While we usually believe that vigilance is a prerequisite for clarity of thinking or for problem resolution (e.g., Levy's sleep-in-the-sleep thinking), we usually do not think that sleeping or dreaming is a state of vigilance, so we may not say that he was alert at the time. Is he conscious when he writes his own thoughts, because he finds himself unable to read them the next morning? He is conscious enough to get pens and paper, and we usually believe that one must be conscious to carry out such targeted behaviour. But if he was conscious when writing his thoughts, why was he unable to understand what he was writing the next day?

p5.original: 你是否曾在梦中对某件事情有了某个想法，或者想出了解决某个问题的办法？如果是，这是否意味着我们在做梦时是有意识的？这可能是认知心理学中最容易引起争议的问题之一。
p5.en: Have you ever thought about something in your dream or figured out a way to solve a problem? If so, does that mean that we are conscious in our dreams? This is probably one of the most controversial issues in cognitive psychology.

p6.original: 这一令人费解的例子说明了在定义“有意识”究竟意味着什么时，心理学家偶尔会遇到的困难。问题在于意识是如此主观和难以捉摸，就像寻找彩虹的尽头一样（Damasio，1999，2000）。在19世纪末，当结构主义者（structuralist）试图剖析意识体验时，这个难题首次出现。你可能还记得，他们使用了一种被称作“内省”（introspection）的简单技术，要求人们报告他们自己的意识体验。几乎每个人都可以迅速地认识到意识的不稳定性和主观性，于是心理学家开始绝望，以为永远找不到科学方法来客观地研究像意识体验这样隐秘的事物。（想一想，你怎么证明你具有意识。）
p6.en: This inexplicable example illustrates the occasional difficulties experienced by psychologists in defining what “conscious” means. The problem is that consciousness is so subjective and elusive, just as it looks at the end of the rainbow (Damasio, 1999, 2000). In the end of the nineteenth century, when structuralists attempted to analyze their conscious experiences, this difficulty first emerged. You may recall that they use a simple technique called Introspection, which requires people to report on their own conscious experiences. Almost everyone quickly realized the precariousness and subjectivity of consciousness, and the psychologist began to despair that there would never be a scientific way to objectively study something as secret as the experience of consciousness. (Think about how you prove you're conscious. I don't think so.

p7.original: 解决这个问题困难重重，以至于在20世纪初，臭名昭著而又颇具影响的行为主义者约翰·华生宣称，心智超出了年轻的心理科学的研究范围。他声称，心理过程只不过是我们行为的副产品。例如，你不是因悲伤而哭泣，你很悲伤是因为有些事情让你哭泣。在华生的指引下，心理学变成了简单的行为科学。因此，当时的心理学不仅失去了其意识，还失去了其心智！
p7.en: It is difficult to resolve this problem so that, at the beginning of the twentieth century, the notorious and influential actor John Watson claimed that the mind went beyond the research of young psychosciences. He claims that the psychological process is simply a by-product of our behaviour. For example, you are not crying out of grief, you are sad because there are things that make you cry. Under Watson's guidance, psychology has become a simple behavioural science. As a result, the psychology at the time lost not only its consciousness but also its mind!

p8.original: 意识心理学一直处于停滞状态，直到20世纪60年代，认知心理学家、神经科学家和计算机科学家组成了联盟，使其重获生机（Gardner，1985）。他们这样做有以下两个原因。
p8.en: Conscious psychology remained stagnant until the 1960s, when a coalition of cognitive psychologists, neuroscientists and computer scientists was formed to revive it (Gardner, 1985). They did so for two reasons.

p9.original: 1. 许多心理学问题浮出水面，需要给出比行为主义更好的解释：记忆的奇闻趣事、知觉的错觉和药物诱发的状态（这在20世纪60年代非常普遍）。
p9.en: 1. Many psychological problems surfaced and required a better explanation than behaviorism: the strangeness of memory, the illusion of consciousness and the drug-induced state (which was common in the 1960s).

p10.original: 2. 第二个原因是技术的发展。科学家开发出了新的工具，尤其是计算机，这使得脑部扫描成为可能，并且计算机还提供了一个模型，可以解释大脑如何加工信息。
p10.en: 2. The second reason is technological development. Scientists have developed new tools, especially computers, which make brain scans possible, and computers also provide a model to explain how the brain processes information.

p11.original: 此后，新工具和未解决的问题促使了多学科间的共同努力，一门新的学科因此诞生了，它被称为认知神经科学（cognitive neuroscience）。认知神经科学吸引了来自不同领域的科学家，他们开始着手去揭示大脑如何加工信息和形成意识经验的奥秘。从认知神经科学的角度来看，大脑就像一个拥有大量资源的生物计算设备，其中有1000亿个类似于晶体管的神经元，每个神经元都有成千上万个连接，可以形成复杂的想象世界和被我们视为意识的体验（Chalmers，1995）。
p11.en: Since then, new tools and unresolved issues have led to a concerted multidisciplinary effort, resulting in the birth of a new discipline known as cognition neuroscience. Cognitive neurosciences have attracted scientists from different fields who have begun to reveal the mystery of how the brain processes information and creates conscious experience. From the perspective of cognitive neuroscience, the brain is like a biocalculating device with vast resources, with 100 billion neurons like transistors, each of which has thousands of connections that can create a complex imagination of the world and the experience of what we see as consciousness (Charmers, 1995).

p12.original: 总体而言，有意识心理可以承担各种角色。但是有意识心理必须从一个事物到另一个事物依次聚焦，如同移动的聚光灯（Tononi & Edelman，1998）。意识不擅长同时处理多个任务，所以，如果你试图边开车边用手机发短信，那么你就必须在两个任务之间来回转移你的注意力（Rubenstein et al.，2001；Strayer et al.，2003）。与此同时，非意识过程（nonconscious processes）则没有这种限制，可以同时进行多个任务，这就是为什么你可以边走路边嚼口香糖，同时还在呼吸。用更专业的术语来说，意识必须有序地加工信息，而非意识的脑回路则可以并行地加工多个信息流。因此，这引出了我们的核心概念：
p12.en: Generally speaking, there are various roles that conscious minds can assume. But conscious psychology must focus on one thing in turn, like a moving spotlight (Tononi & Edelman, 1998). Consciousness is not good at dealing with multiple tasks at the same time, so if you try to drive and text with your cell phone, you have to shift your attention between the two missions (Rubenstein et al., 2001); Strayer et al., 2003). At the same time, the non-conscious processes do not have such limitations and can be accompanied by multiple missions, which is why you can chew gum while walking and breathing. In more professional terms, consciousness must process information in an orderly manner, while a mind-to-heart circuit that is not conscious can process multiple information streams in parallel. Thus, this brings into play our core concept:

p13.original: 大脑同时在意识和无意识的多个水平上运作。
p13.en: The brain operates at multiple levels, both conscious and unconscious.

p14.original: 让我们回到我们在这一学习阶段开始时提出的问题：意识（consciousness）究竟是什么？由于认知神经科学的发展，现在我们不再将意识定义为一种存在状态，而将其定义为形成我们对世界的心理表征和我们的当前想法的大脑过程。将其视为一个过程，承认了意识是动态的和连续的，而非静止的和离散的。并且，它是一个与我们研究过的其他心理过程相关的加工过程，这些心理过程包括学习、记忆、注意和感知觉（见图8-1）。
p14.en: Let us return to the question we asked at the beginning of this learning phase: what is consciousness? As a result of the development of cognitive neurosciences, we now no longer define consciousness as a state of existence, but rather as a brain process that shapes our psychological manifestations of the world and our current thinking. It is seen as a process that recognizes that awareness is dynamic and continuous, rather than static and discrete. Moreover, it is a process associated with other psychological processes that we have studied, including learning, memory, attention and perception (see figure 8-1).

p15.original: 图8-1 意识与许多大脑加工过程相关
p15.en: Figure 8-1 Awareness related to many brain processes

p16.original: 注：意识与学习、记忆、注意和感知觉相关。
p16.en: Note: Consciousness is associated with learning, memory, attention and sensory.

p17.original: 例如，进入意识的一切事物都会经过工作记忆（working memory）。当感觉刺激获得我们的注意并从感觉记忆进入工作记忆时，我们就对它有了意识。因此，也可以说，我们对进入工作记忆的一切事物都有意识。所以，一些心理学家认为，工作记忆实际上就是人们一直在寻找的意识的所在地（Engle，2002；LeDoux，1996）。
p17.en: For example, everything that enters consciousness goes through working memory. We're conscious of it when it's the feeling that stimulates our attention and brings it to work. Therefore, we can also say that we are conscious of everything that enters into the work memory. Thus, some psychologists believe that working memory is in fact the place of the consciousness that people have been looking for (Engle, 2002); LeDoux, 1996.

p18.original: 意识同样也与学习相关，尽管认知学习和行为学习貌似涉及不同的脑机制。大多数认知学习（如你对本章材料的学习）都依赖于有意识过程。而许多行为学习，尤其是经典条件反射（classical conditioning，如恐惧反应的习得）则在很大程度上依赖于可发生在意识之外的心理过程。
p18.en: Awareness is also relevant to learning, although cognitive learning and behavioural learning seem to involve different brain mechanisms. Most cognitive learning (e.g. your study of this chapter) relies on conscious processes. Many behavioral learning, especially classic reflections (such as the acquisition of fear reactions), depend heavily on psychological processes that can occur outside the consciousness.

p19.original: 另一个与意识相关的心理过程是注意（attention），它的特征是使一个项目从意识中的其他项目中脱颖而出，就像有人在拥挤的房间里喊你的名字一样。注意使你能够在吵闹的背景中跟着你当下正进行的对话的思路走（心理学家称之为选择性注意或鸡尾酒会现象）。而注意又与感觉（sensation）和知觉（perception）的双重加工密切相关，包括疼痛知觉（该心理过程与意识的关系尚未完全为人们所知）。在本章后面的部分，我们将探讨意识状态（如催眠）如何有效地控制疼痛。
p19.en: Another awareness-related psychological process is Attention, which is characterized by the emergence of a project from other projects in the consciousness, like someone who calls out your name in crowded rooms. Take care to follow the lines of dialogue you are having in the context of the noise (what psychologists call selective attention or cocktail parties). Attention is also closely related to the dual processing of feelings and perceptions, including pain perception (the relationship between the psychological process and consciousness is not yet fully known). At the end of this chapter, we will explore how the state of consciousness (e.g. hypnosis) can be effective in controlling pain.

p20.original: 关于意识的作用的最后一点是：它可以帮助你把现实和幻想结合起来，并在你的脑海中形成连续播放的“电影”。例如，当你在饥饿时看到一个甜甜圈，你的工作记忆会（基于感觉和知觉）形成一个甜甜圈的有意识表象，并在查询长时记忆（long-term memory，得益于行为学习）后，将表象与食物联系起来，最后让你想象吃甜甜圈的样子。由此看出，意识依赖于我们所讨论过的全部心理过程。但大脑究竟是如何做到这一点的呢？这也许是心理学中最大的奥秘。数十亿神经元的放电模式如何成为甜甜圈的有意识表象（或者这页纸上的文字和观点的表象）呢？
p20.en: The final point about the role of consciousness is that it can help you to combine reality with fantasy and to form a continuous “film” in your mind. For example, when you see a doughnut when you're hungry, your work memory forms a conscious image of a doughnut (based on feeling and consciousness) and, after searching for long-term memory (long-term memory, thanks to behavioral learning), connects it to food, and finally makes you imagine eating a doughnut. It follows that consciousness depends on the entire psychological process that we have discussed. But how exactly does the brain do that? It's probably the biggest mystery of psychology. How does the multibillion-billion neurons discharge model become a conscious appearance of a donut (or of words and views on this page)?

p22.original: 8.1 描述用于研究意识的技术。
p22.en: 8.1 Description of technologies for research awareness.

p23.original: 8.2 回顾用于审视有意识和无意识的心理模型。
p23.en: 8.2 Review of conscious and unconscious psychological models.

p24.original: 8.3 描述科学家对昏迷中的意识及相关状态的认识。
p24.en: 8.3 Describes scientists ' awareness of the unconscious and related state.

p27.original: 描述用于研究意识的技术。
p27.en: Description of technology for research awareness.

p28.original: 高科技工具，如fMRI、PET和EEG[1]，打开了通往大脑的新窗口，使研究人员能够看到在各种不同心理任务中哪些脑区处于活跃状态。换句话说，我们可以辨认出意识中的一些内容是“什么”：虽然这些成像设备尚不能揭示意识体验的实际内容，但它们确实指出了我们在阅读、说话或转移注意时，所“点亮”的不同的大脑结构群（见图8-2）。
p28.en: High-tech tools, such as fMRI, PET and EEG [1], open new windows to the brain, enabling researchers to see which brain regions are active in different psychological missions. In other words, we can identify some of the elements of the consciousness as “what”: while these imaging devices do not yet reveal the actual content of the conscious experience, they do point to different brain structures that we “light” when reading, talking or diverting attention (see figure 8-2).

p29.original: 图8-2 对工作中大脑的PET扫描
p29.en: Figure 8-2 PET scan of the working brain

p30.original: 注：这些PET扫描显示了大脑的不同区域如何在不同的有意识任务中变得活跃起来。
p30.en: Note: These PET scans show how different regions of the brain become active in different conscious missions.

p31.original: 毫无疑问，这些结果图像表明，有意识加工涉及多个脑回路的同时活动，尤其是连接丘脑和大脑皮层的皮层通路。但是，为了认识其潜在的心理过程（意识如何运作），心理学家发明了其他更为巧妙的技术。在本章中，我们将看到其中的许多技术，并且这些技术会贯穿全书。不过，下面我们会先给出两个例子，用其预告即将到来的精彩内容。
p31.en: Undoubtedly, the results show that conscious processing involves simultaneous activity involving multiple brain circuits, especially the cortical route linking the cortex and the cortex of the brain. However, in order to understand their potential psychological processes (how the consciousness works), psychologists have developed other, more sophisticated techniques. In this chapter, we will see many of these technologies, and they will permeate the book. However, we will begin with two examples that will be used as a preview of the upcoming highlights.

p33.original: 罗杰·谢泼德（Roger Shepard）和杰奎琳·梅茨勒（Jacqueline Metzler）的一项经典实验表明，当人们谈及在头脑中“翻转物体”时，这不仅仅是一个比喻（Shepard & Metzler，1971）。使用那些类似于图8-3的图画，谢泼德和梅茨勒要求志愿者判断每对图像是否显示的是不同视角下的同一物体。
p33.en: A classic experiment by Roger Shepard and Jacqueline Metzler shows that when people talk about “vert objects” in their minds, this is not just a metaphor (Shepard & Metzler, 1971). Using graphics similar to figures 8-3, Shepherd and Metzler asked volunteers to judge whether each pair of images showed the same object from different perspectives.

p35.original: 注：你认为每对图像是否显示的是不同位置的同一物体？这三对中是否有一对更容易得出答案？
p35.en: Note: Do you think each image displays the same object in different positions? Is it easier to get answers from one of these three pairs?

p37.original: 谢泼德和梅茨勒假设，如果大脑在比较图像时确实会进行图像旋转，那么当成对图像之间的角度差异越大时，人们会花费越长的时间来做出反应。他们是正确的。你得出A的答案是否比B或C的更快？
p37.en: Shepherd and Metzler assume that if the brain does rotate images when comparing them, it will take longer to react as the angle between images becomes more different. They're right. Did you get A's answer faster than B or C?

p39.original: 另一种巧妙方法则另辟蹊径地探究了意识“如何运行”：斯蒂芬·科斯林（Stephen Kosslyn，1976）发现，我们可以使用我们的有意识心理“放大”心理表象的细节，就像照相机一样。为了证明这一点，科斯林（Kosslyn，1976）首先要求被试想象物体，如大象、猫或椅子等。然后，他会询问被试有关所想象物体的细节问题（例如，“它是一只黑猫吗”或“它有长尾巴吗”），并记录被试回答问题所用的时间。他发现，询问的细节越小，被试做出反应所需要的时间就越长。科斯林指出，这是因为人们需要额外的时间来更为仔细地检查他们的心理表象。
p39.en: Another clever way of looking at the conscious "how to run": Stephen Kosslyn, 1976, found that we could use the details of our conscious mental "magnifying" psychological appearances, like a camera. To prove this, Kosslyn, 1976, first requires that objects such as elephants, cats or chairs be tried. He would then ask questions about the details of the object being tried (e.g. “Is it a black cat” or “Does it have a long tail”) and record the time taken to be tried to answer the question. He found that the smaller the details asked, the longer it would take to be tried to react. Koslin stated that this was because people needed additional time to examine their psychological symptoms more closely.

p40.original: 试一试 放大心理表象

p41.original: 请你的一位朋友闭上眼睛，想象一座房子。然后让你的朋友描述屋顶、房门和门铃按钮的颜色。使用显示秒数的手表或时钟，记录得到每个答案所用的时间。基于科斯林的研究，你预计哪一个问题所需的反应时最长？哪一个最短？
p41.en: One of your friends would close his eyes and imagine a house. Then let your friends describe the color of the roof, the door and the doorbell button. The time taken to obtain each answer is recorded using a watch or clock showing the seconds. Based on Coslin's research, which question do you expect to have the longest response? Which one's the shortest?

p42.original: 你可能会发现，询问的细节越小，你的朋友做出反应所需要的时间就越长。科斯林将此解释为人们需要额外的时间来“放大”心理表象，以解析较小的特征。换句话说，我们以审视外部世界中自然物体的方式来审视我们的心理表象，以感知“全貌”或细节。
p42.en: You might find that the smaller the question, the longer your friend takes to react. Coslin interpreted this to mean that people need additional time to “expand” the symptoms of the symptoms in order to analyze the smaller features. In other words, we look at our psychological appearances in a way that looks at natural objects in the outside world, and senses “the whole picture” or details.

p43.original: 正如摄影师需要更长时间来放大一个小细节一样，我们也需要更多时间来放大我们心理表象中的较小细节。
p43.en: Just as photographers need longer to magnify a small detail, we need more time to magnify the smaller detail in our psychological appearance.

p44.original: 这两个实验都表明我们会有意识地操纵我们的视觉表象。并且我们做到这一点的方式与我们操纵外部世界中自然物体的方式大致相同（Kosslyn，2005）。随着本章的进行，你将了解到神经科学家研究意识及其相关心理过程时所使用的其他技术。不过，先让我们较为仔细地了解一些心理模型。
p44.en: Both experiments show that we will consciously manipulate our visual appearances. And we do this in the same way as we manipulate natural objects in the outside world (Kosslyn, 2005). As this chapter proceeds, you will learn about the other techniques used by neuroscientists in their research awareness and their associated psychological processes. However, let us first get a closer look at some psychological models.

p45.original: 8.2 有意识和无意识的心理模型

p47.original: 回顾用于审视有意识和无意识的心理模型。
p47.en: A review of conscious and unconscious psychological models.

p48.original: 随着心理学家致力于意识的研究和理解，出现了几种至今仍然有用的模型。解决问题的方式多种多样，其中一种有用的策略是寻找类比。心理学家采用了这一策略，试图通过寻找表征这个难以捉摸的概念的最佳隐喻，来刻画意识的本质。
p48.en: As psychologists are committed to the study and understanding of awareness, several models have emerged that are still useful to date. The way in which the problem is solved is varied, and one useful strategy is to find analogies. This strategy is used by psychologists who attempt to paint the nature of the consciousness by looking for the best metaphor for this elusive concept.

p50.original: 西格蒙德·弗洛伊德最早提出了一个被当下许多人都认为理所当然的观念：我们的心理同时在多个水平上运作。他把意识比作冰山一角，这表明还有很大一部分存在于水面之下。弗洛伊德认为，存在于水面之下的部分——无意识（unconscious）——是存贮需求、欲望、愿望和创伤性记忆的容器。此外，他还认为，无意识加工（在我们意识之外的加工）可以影响我们有意识的思想、感受、梦境、幻想和行为。现在，大量证据证实了弗洛伊德的这一见解，即大部分心理运作会潜藏在看不见的地方，即在意识水平之下（见图8-4）。
p50.en: Sigmund Freud first put forward a concept that is now taken for granted by many: that our psychology operates at multiple levels. He compared consciousness to the tip of the iceberg, which showed that a significant portion of it existed below the water surface. In Freud's view, the part that exists below the surface — unconscious (unconscious) — is a container for storage of demand, desire, desire and traumatic memories. Moreover, he believes that unconscious processing (examining our consciousness) can affect our conscious thoughts, feelings, dreams, illusions and behaviours. There is now ample evidence to support Freud's view that most psychological operations are hidden in invisible places, that is, at the level of consciousness (see figure 8-4).

p51.original: 图8-4 弗洛伊德的意识水平模型

p52.original: 注：弗洛伊德用冰山作为人类心理的隐喻，指出我们的有意识心理是最小的一部分，就像冰山一角。
p52.en: Note: Freud uses the iceberg as a metaphor for the human mind, pointing out that our conscious mind is the smallest part, just like the tip of the iceberg.

p53.original: 前意识 心理学家经常使用弗洛伊德的术语“前意识”（preconscious）来指代对事件（如去年你的生日会）和事实（塞勒姆是俄勒冈州的首府）的记忆，尽管这些记忆没有立即进入意识，但会很容易到达意识。当有事物提示人们进行回忆时，这些记忆就可以相对容易地进入意识。否则，它们会一直存在于心底，刚好在意识的边界之外，直至需要时它们才进入意识。因此，在现代认知的意义上，前意识与长时记忆很相似。
p53.en: Ex-Sensitization Psychologists often use the Freconscioous term to refer to the memory of events (such as last year's birthday party) and facts (the capital of Oregon), which are easy to reach, even though they are not immediately conscious. When there is something that reminds people, it is relatively easy for them to enter their minds. Otherwise, they will remain at the bottom of the heart, just outside the boundaries of consciousness and only when needed. Thus, in the modern sense of perception, the preconscious is very similar to the long-term memory.

p54.original: 前意识加工既有优点，又有缺点。
p54.en: Pre-awareness processes have both advantages and disadvantages.

p55.original: 一方面，它不受意识序列的、一次只做一件事的限制。因此，它可以同时在多个地方搜索信息，这种能力被称作并行加工（parallel processing）。
p55.en: On the one hand, it is not subject to a conscious sequence of one thing at a time. Thus, it can search for information in multiple places at the same time, and this capability is called parallel processing (parallel processing).

p56.original: 另一方面，前意识缺乏意识所具有的深思熟虑的能力。你可以将前意识想象为一个记忆仓库，其中的库存在不停地转动，以使最近使用的和最情绪化的信息最容易被获取。
p56.en: On the other hand, there is a lack of considered capacity for pre-consciousness. You can imagine the former consciousness as a memory warehouse, where stocks are constantly shifting so that the most recently used and emotional information is most easily available.

p57.original: 无意识 词典可能会将无意识这一术语定义为全部意识的缺失，如人在晕厥、昏迷或处于麻醉时的状态。然而，弗洛伊德将无意识定义为隐藏于意识之外的贮存着原始动机和威胁性记忆的容器。认知心理学家认为无意识还有另一个含义，即指大脑中产生的任何形式的无意识加工过程（包括呼吸、转头等）。把这些概念结合在一起，我们将无意识定义为一个广义的术语，它指的是意识水平之下的多个加工水平。其范围很广：从前意识记忆到控制基本躯体机能的脑活动，再到当我们形成对桌子或朋友所发评论的知觉时其背后运行的过程。这些无意识过程可能很微妙，会在我们没有意识到的情况下导致焦虑或抑郁（Kihlstrom，1987）。
p57.en: Unconscious Dictionary may define the term unconscious as a complete lack of consciousness, such as a person in a state of faintness, coma or anaesthesia. However, Freud defined unconsciousness as a container that stored original motives and threatening memories hidden from consciousness. Cognitive psychologists see the additional meaning of unconsciousness as any form of unconscious process (including breathing, turning back, etc.) occurring in the brain. Taken together, we have defined unconsciously as a broad term, which refers to multiple processing levels below the level of awareness. The scope of this is wide: the memory of the brain activity that controls the basic body function, and the process that runs behind it when we form a sense of what we say about the table or friends. These unconscious processes can be subtle and can cause anxiety or depression without our awareness (Kihlstrom, 1987).

p58.original: 如果你想一想自己是如何经常沿着熟悉的路线上班或上学，而无须深思熟虑时（甚至在开车时），你就会了解无意识过程是如何对我们产生影响的。正如你将在下面的演示中看到的那样，我们可以在实验室中研究无意识过程。
p58.en: If you think about how you often go to work or go to school along familiar lines without thinking about it (even when you drive), you know how the unconscious process affects us. As you will see in the demonstration below, we can study unconscious processes in the lab.

p59.original: 试着在下面的空白处填写字母，以将词干补全为一个单词：
p59.en: Try filling in letters in the following blanks to complete the words in one word:

p61.original: 看到空白处时，你的脑海中浮现出了哪个词？
p61.en: When you see a blank, what word does it come out of your head?

p62.original: 一种被称为启动的技术使心理学家可以影响被试对此类问题的回答，但被试并不会意识到自己受到了影响。在刚刚给出的这个例子中，答案有许多可选项，包括defend、defeat、deffect、defile、deform、defray和defuse。我们并不能确切地知道你的答案是什么，但我们的确能让你给出define[2]这个答案。怎么做到的呢？通过在给出问题前多次使用define这个词，我们蓄意“启动”了你的反应（当然，并不能完全确定你会像预期的那样做出反应，只是增加了你那样做的概率）。通过诸如此类的方法，心理学家拥有了强大的工具来探究意识和无意识过程的相互作用。
p62.en: A technique known as activation allows psychologists to influence answers to such questions, but is not aware that they are affected. In this example just given, there are many options for the answers, including Devend, defeat, deffect, defile, deform, defray and defuse. We can't know exactly what your answer is, but we can do that for you. How did you do that? By using the term "definine" several times before giving questions, we deliberately “started” your reaction (of course, it is not entirely certain that you would react as expected, but it increases the probability that you would do so). Through such methods, psychologists have powerful tools to explore the interaction between conscious and unconscious processes.

p64.original: 威廉·詹姆斯（William James）给出了一个不同的隐喻，他把平常清醒的意识比作一条奔涌的河流，携带着不断变化的感觉、知觉、思维、记忆、感受、动机和欲望。这种“意识流”包含对我们自己和环境刺激的觉知。詹姆斯认为，它还可以包含来自内部的躯体感觉，如饥饿、口渴、疼痛和快乐。
p64.en: William James has given a different metaphor, comparing his common sense of consciousness to a river running, carrying changing feelings, consciousness, thinking, memory, feeling, motivation and desire. This “conscious stream” includes a sense of our own and our environmental stimuli. James believes that it can also include body feelings from within, such as hunger, thirst, pain and happiness.

p65.original: 詹姆斯理论的部分内容有点类似于弗洛伊德对意识和前意识的区分。对詹姆斯来说，意识具有两个水平。
p65.en: Part of James' theory is somewhat similar to Freud's distinction between consciousness and preconscious. For James, there are two levels of consciousness.

p66.original: 1. 焦点区域，包括我们在任何特定时间密切关注的任何事物。
p66.en: 1. Focus areas, including anything that we closely observe at any given time.

p67.original: 2. 外周意识，包括为我们的焦点赋予意义和背景的感触和联想。
p67.en: 2. A sense of outreach, including a sense of meaning and context for our focus.

p68.original: 例如，当你参加朋友的婚礼时，你内心的焦点是正在结婚的夫妇以及与你互动的客人。你对婚姻的感受，你所知道的使这对夫妇走到生命中这一关键时刻的所有事情，以及这一事件所引发的任何其他记忆，都是外周意识的一部分，就像戏剧中的配角一样。这样，我们就可以用视觉作为另一个隐喻来描述詹姆斯的意识模型：就像我们的外周视觉一样，我们的外周意识不是我们关注的对象，但却为我们关注的对象提供了意义和背景。
p68.en: For example, when you go to a friend's wedding, your inner focus is on married couples and guests who interact with you. The way you feel about marriage, all that you know that brings the couple to this critical moment in their lives, and any other memory that this event triggers, is part of the outer consciousness, just like the part of the drama. In this way, we can describe James's consciousness model as another metaphor: like our outer vision, our outer consciousness is not the object of our attention, but it provides meaning and context for the object of our concern.

p69.original: 詹姆斯建立了有关两个意识水平的理论。意识的焦点，就像聚光灯下的事物一样，占据了中心位置。然而，我们的外周意识也同等重要：就像聚光灯之外的事物一样，我们的外周意识为经历增添了丰富的细节。
p69.en: James has developed a theory of two levels of consciousness. The focus of consciousness, like what's under the spotlight, is in the center. However, our outer-week consciousness is equally important: just like what goes beyond the spotlight, our outer-week consciousness adds a wealth of detail to the experience.

p71.original: 我们为意识提出的最后一个隐喻来自认知心理学。计算机隐喻把意识比作出现在计算机屏幕上的信息和图像，而无意识过程就像计算机屏幕后内部的电活动。大多数时候，我们的无意识机制都会无声无息地与意识并行运作，但偶尔无意识动机或情绪会变得如此强烈以至于其会在意识中爆发。例如，当一种与情绪性记忆相关的特殊气味突然把这一情绪带入思维的中心时，或者当饥饿的驱力逐渐增强并闯入意识时。
p71.en: Our last metaphor for consciousness comes from cognitive psychology. Computer metaphors compare consciousness to the information and images that are now on the computer screen, while unconscious processes are like electrical activity inside the computer screen. Most of the time, our unconscious mechanisms operate in silence in parallel with consciousness, but occasionally unconscious motivations or emotions become so powerful that they erupt into consciousness. For example, when a special scent associated with emotional memory suddenly brings it to the centre of thinking, or when the driving force of hunger increases and breaks into consciousness.

p72.original: 所有这些隐喻都可以帮助我们理解意识的本质，而随着我们对这一令人着迷的过程的理解不断深入，我们将在本章中定期回顾它们。不过，在结束本节内容之前，让我们再问一个重要问题：为什么意识如此重要？
p72.en: All of these metaphors can help us understand the essence of consciousness, and as our understanding of this fascinating process deepens, we will periodically review them in this chapter. Before concluding this section, however, let us ask another important question: why is awareness so important?

p73.en: 8.2.4 What does consciousness do to us?

p74.original: 此时此刻，你的意识正专注于这些白底黑字，但是这些文字并不是孤立的。就像詹姆斯在他关于外周意识的讨论中所指出的那样，这些词语具有意义，当你阅读的时候这些意义会在意识中流动。当然，你可以把注意的聚光灯转移到其他事物上（也许是背景音乐），当你这样做时，纸张上的词语就会滑入意识的边缘。你可能会在纸张上移动你的目光，而未实际加工其含义（相信每个读者都有过这种经历）。
p74.en: At this moment, your mind is focused on these white and black words, but they are not isolated. As James pointed out in his discussion on outer space consciousness, these words have meaning, and they flow in the consciousness when you read. Of course, you can turn the spotlight to other things (perhaps background music), and when you do that, the words on the paper slide to the edge of your consciousness. You may move your eyes on paper without actually processing the meaning (believing that every reader has such an experience).

p75.original: 现在，如果我们能再次引起你的注意，我们想提醒你，意识具有许多功能。上一段落中的场景说明了意识的三个特别重要的功能（Solso，2001；Tononi & Edelman，1998）。
p75.en: Now, if we can get your attention again, we would like to remind you that consciousness has many functions. The scene in the preceding paragraph illustrates three particularly important functions of awareness (Soliso, 2001); Tononi & Edelman, 1998.

p76.original: 意识限制了我们的注意。因为意识会序列加工信息，所以它限制了你所注意和思考的内容。通过这种方式，意识可以防止你的大脑被刺激淹没。不幸的是，当你把注意转移到背景音乐或新的短信上时，意识一次只做一件事的属性会让你不再专注于正在阅读的内容。这也解释了为什么在开车时使用手机会大大增加车祸的风险。
p76.en: Consciousness limits our attention. Because consciousness processes information in sequence, it limits the content of your attention and reflection. In this way, consciousness can prevent your brain from being inundated with stimulation. Unfortunately, when you shift attention to background music or new text messages, the attributes of consciousness to do one thing at a time will make you lose focus on what you are reading. This also explains why the use of hand opportunities in driving significantly increases the risk of car accidents.

p77.original: 意识提供了一个心理“会场”。在这里，感觉可以与记忆、情绪、动机以及许多其他心理过程相结合，我们称这一过程为知觉。因此，意识就像画布，通常我们会在这块画布上根据内外部世界提供的刺激调色板创造出有意义的图画。这是意识的一个方面，它将纸张上的词语与其意义联系起来，或者将看到老朋友的面孔与喜悦的情绪联系起来。实际上，神经成像研究表明，意识的本质是在大脑的不同部位之间建立联系（Massimini et al.，2005）。因此，意识处于认知的核心。
p77.en: Consciousness provides a psychological “meeting place”. Here, feelings can be combined with memories, emotions, motivations and many other psychological processes, which we call consciousness. So consciousness is like a canvas, and we usually create meaningful drawings on this canvas based on the stimulating palettes that the inside and outside world provides. This is an aspect of consciousness, which links the words on paper to their meaning or to the feelings of joy when seeing an old friend. In fact, neuroimaging studies show that the essence of consciousness is the connection between different parts of the brain (Massimini et al., 2005). Awareness is therefore at the core of awareness.

p78.original: 意识使我们形成了认识世界的心理模型，一个我们可以在头脑中操纵的模型。与较简单的有机体不同，意识使我们不必成为当下的囚徒：我们不只会对刺激做出反射性反应。相反，我们使用对世界的有意识模型，凭借记忆和事先的思考，把过去和未来都带入意识中。利用这个模型，我们可以通过操纵我们的心理世界来进行思考和规划，以评估可供选择的反应并想象它们的有效性。例如，正是意识的这一特征帮助你在本文中的概念和自己的经历之间建立联系，或者阻止你对穿着你不喜欢的衣服的朋友残忍地说出实话。
p78.en: Awareness has led us to a psychological model of understanding the world, a model that we can manipulate in our minds. Unlike simpler organisms, consciousness does not make us prisoners: we do not just react to irritation. Rather, we use conscious models of the world, with memory and prior thinking, to bring the past and the future into our consciousness. Using this model, we can think and plan by manipulating our psychological world to assess alternative responses and imagine their effectiveness. For example, it is this characteristic of consciousness that helps you to establish a link between the concept in this paper and your own experience, or to prevent you from telling the truth in cold blood to your friend in a dress you don't like.

p79.original: 限制、结合和操纵这三个功能，在不同程度上适用于所有的意识状态，无论是做梦、催眠、冥想、药物诱发的状态，还是我们“正常”的觉醒状态。但是，被称为昏迷的状态又是怎样的呢？其符合我们对意识的研究吗？
p79.en: Limiting, combining and manipulating these three functions apply to all states of consciousness to varying degrees, be they dreamt, hypnotized, meditated, drug-induced or our “normal” state of awakening. But what's the state of the coma? Is it consistent with our study of consciousness?

p82.original: 描述科学家对昏迷中的意识及相关状态的认识。
p82.en: Describes scientists ' awareness of unconsciousness and related state.

p83.original: 公众对昏迷（coma）的含义存在重大的误解。这种误解部分源于一些高度曝光的情感案例，这些案例引发了有关是否停止对严重脑损伤患者的生命支持的伦理问题的激烈讨论（Meyers，2007）。有关“奇迹般”康复案例的报道也在煽风点火。那么事实是怎样的呢？
p83.en: There is a major public misunderstanding about the meaning of coma. This misperception stems in part from highly exposed emotional cases that have led to intense discussions on whether to stop supporting the lives of patients with severe brain damage (Meyers, 2007). Reports of “magic” rehabilitation cases are also fuelling. So what's the truth?

p85.original: 昏迷不是稳定的长期状态。相反，它通常只在脑损伤后持续几天或几周的时间。在昏迷状态下，患者缺乏正常的睡眠和觉醒周期，他们的眼睛通常会保持闭合，不能被唤醒。那些有所好转并进入最小意识状态的患者，可能会拥有有限的意识和大脑工作能力。恢复通常是渐进的（National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke，2007）。那些没有好转的患者会恶化为植物人状态。在这种情况下，他们可能会周期性地睁开眼睛，进入和退出正常的睡眠周期，但他们只有最低限度的脑活动和基本反射。从植物人状态完全恢复正常的机会非常渺茫。
p85.en: A coma is not a stable long-term state. Instead, it usually lasts only a few days or weeks after the brain damage. In a coma, patients lack normal sleep and awakening cycles, and their eyes are usually kept closed and cannot be awakened. Those who improve and enter the state of minimal awareness may have limited consciousness and brain ability to work. Recovery is usually gradual (National Institute of Natural Disorders and Stroke, 2007). Those who are not getting better will turn into vegetable. In such cases, they may open their eyes periodically, enter and exit normal sleep cycles, but they have only minimal brain activity and basic reflections. The chances of a complete return to normality from the state of the botanical people are very remote.

p86.original: 但是，对植物人状态的诊断有时是不准确的，因为对脑活动的测量并不是一门完美的科学。当这种诊断被用于决定是否继续提供生命支持时，误诊可能会导致致命的错误。不过，人们正在开发前景广阔的新型脑成像技术，它们可以更准确地识别看似处于植物人状态的患者的脑活动和意识水平。最近，PET和MRI技术的进步使得研究人员能够成功预测哪些处于植物人状态的患者会有所好转并进入最小意识状态（Owen et al.，2009）。
p86.en: However, the diagnosis of the state of the botanical people is sometimes inaccurate, as the measurement of brain activity is not a perfect science. When such diagnosis is used to determine whether life support continues to be provided, misdiagnostic diagnosis can lead to fatal errors. However, new and promising brain imaging techniques are being developed that can more accurately identify the levels of brain activity and awareness of patients who appear to be in a plant-human condition. Recent advances in PET and MRI technology have enabled researchers to predict successfully which patients in vegetative status will improve and move into a minimal state of consciousness (Owen et al., 2009).

p87.original: 8.3.2 昏迷的人能听到你的声音吗
p87.en: 8.3.2 Can a man in a coma hear your voice?

p88.original: 更令人兴奋的是，一项新研究所引用的证据清楚地表明，如果心爱之人与昏迷中的患者交谈，那么患者（甚至处于植物人状态的患者）则更有可能恢复意识。芝加哥西北大学的神经科学家特蕾莎·帕佩（Theresa Pape）对处于植物人状态和最小意识状态的患者进行了一项随机的安慰剂对照组研究，该研究从患者脑损伤后约两个月开始。患者的家人和朋友录制了患者生活中熟悉的故事，科学家每天都会通过耳机向患者播放四次这些故事，持续六周。研究人员使用MRI扫描发现，当患者听到他们心爱之人讲故事和叫他们的名字时，他们的大脑中与长时记忆及语言加工相关的区域的活动会增加。并且这一现象出现得很快（大部分效应出现在研究的前两周），表明这种治疗刺激了脑活动，帮助患者恢复了较高水平的意识（Pape et al.，2015）。短短几周内，他们就开始更快地清醒过来，更能意识到周围的环境，甚至能够对对话和指令做出反应。帕佩认为，这种治疗对中风患者和颅脑外伤患者都有效，并建议家属与医疗团队使用这种疗法作为患者正在接受的其他形式的治疗的补充。
p88.en: More excitingly, the evidence cited by a new research institute clearly shows that if a person in love talks to a person in a coma, the patient (or even a person in a vegetative state) is more likely to regain consciousness. Theresa Pape, a neuroscientist at Northwestern University in Chicago, conducted a random placebo control group study for patients in plant-human and minimal-conscious conditions, which began about two months after the patient's brain damage. Families and friends of patients record stories familiar to their lives, and scientists broadcast them four times a day through headphones to patients, lasting six weeks. Researchers use MRI scans to find that when patients hear their loved ones tell stories and call their names, there will be an increase in activities in the regions of their brain associated with long-term memory and language processing. And the phenomenon is very rapid (most of the effects occurred in the first two weeks of the study), indicating that the treatment stimulates brain activity and helps patients regain a high level of awareness (Pape et al., 2015). In just a few weeks, they began to wake up faster, more aware of the surrounding environment and even able to react to dialogue and directives. According to Papi, this treatment is effective for both stroke and brain trauma patients, and it is recommended that families and medical teams use it as a complement to other forms of treatment that patients are receiving.

p89.original: 最新研究表明，处于植物人状态的人们也许能够感知到外部刺激，如听到心爱之人的声音。因此，这些意识状态可能就像被困在了不透明的玻璃的后面。这些最新的研究发现为突破意识的障碍提供了希望。
p89.en: Recent studies have shown that people in plant-based situations may be able to sense external incentives, such as hearing the voices of loved ones. Therefore, these state of consciousness may be like being trapped behind a glass that is not transparent. These latest studies have found that there is hope for breaking the barriers to consciousness.

p90.original: 心理学很有用 运用心理学来学习心理学
p90.en: Psychology is useful. Use psychology to learn psychology.

p91.original: 想扩展你的意识吗？在最严格的意义上，这是不可能的，因为意识的容量是有限的。正如我们前面曾指出的那样，意识一次只能专注于一件事。然而，可以扩展的是你的意识能够获取的存储于前意识记忆中的信息。学会如何做到这一点，对需要吸收大量信息并通过考试来证明这一点的学生来说，将大有帮助。
p91.en: Want to expand your consciousness? In the strictest sense, this is not possible because the capacity of consciousness is limited. As we have stated before, awareness can only focus on one thing at a time. What can be expanded, however, is the information that your consciousness can access that is stored in the memory of your predecessor. Learning how to do this would be of great assistance to students who need to absorb a great deal of information and pass an examination to prove it.

p92.original: 当然，在面临考试时，学生有时会“通宵”学习，如果你的意识没有因为通宵学习造成睡眠缺乏而受损，那么你就会具有优势。再多的咖啡因也无法使你缺乏睡眠的意识恢复至最佳状态，正如你的老师一直不厌其烦地劝诫你的那样（也正如记忆研究所表明的那样），把你的学习内容分散至数日或数周比尝试一次性学完要好得多。所以，这就是增加你的前意识中的内容通达意识的第一个技巧！
p92.en: Of course, in the face of exams, students sometimes “nightly” learning, and if your consciousness is not damaged by sleep deprivation caused by overnight learning, you will have the advantage. More caffeine will not restore your sense of lack of sleep to your best state, as your teacher has been constantly exhorting you (as the Memory Institute has shown) to spread your learning to days or weeks better than to try to complete one-time studies. So, this is the first technique to increase your awareness of what you're thinking before!

p93.original: 由于意识的容量极其有限，你不可能把考试需要记住的所有内容都保持在意识中。这些材料必须被存储在容易获取但又处于意识之外的前意识的长时记忆中。技巧在于能够在需要时将其带回意识。以下是一些更有用的策略。
p93.en: Because of the extremely limited capacity of consciousness, it is not possible for you to keep in mind all the elements that need to be kept in mind in the examination. These materials must be stored in long-term memories of pre-consciousness, which is easily accessible but is also out of consciousness. The technique is to be able to bring it back to consciousness when needed. Here are some of the more useful strategies.

p94.original: 与学习伙伴或学习小组讨论概念有助于提高你对材料的有意识理解。
p94.en: The concept of working with learning partners or learning groups helps to increase your conscious understanding of the material.

p95.original: 1. 练习精细复述。学生有时认为他们的教授会问“刁钻的问题”（尽管教授几乎从未故意这样做过）。实际上，一道好的考题能表明学生是否真正理解了一个术语的含义，而非仅仅记住一个定义。通过用你自己的话来表述定义，然后从你自己的生活中想出一个例子，你将对这个概念形成更丰富的记忆，从而使其更容易从你的前意识中提取出来。
p95.en: Practice detail. Students sometimes think that their professors will ask “the question of the street” (although the professor has almost never done it intentionally). Indeed, a good test would indicate whether students really understood the meaning of a term, rather than simply remembering a definition. By using your own words to define it, and by coming up with an example from your own life, you will have a richer memory of the concept, making it easier to extract it from your former consciousness.

p96.original: 2. 寻找概念之间的联系。一旦你理解了这些概念，你还需要知道这些概念是如何相互联系的。例如，你的教授可能会要求你解释意识和前意识之间的关系。因此，一个不错的学习策略是问问你自己这个新的概念（如前意识）与之前已学习过的其他概念（如意识或无意识）有何联系。
p96.en: 2. Finding conceptual linkages. Once you have understood these concepts, you need to know how they relate. For example, your professor may ask you to explain the relationship between consciousness and pre-consciousness. So a good learning strategy is to ask yourself how this new concept (e.g., the former consciousness) is related to other concepts that have been learned before (e.g., consciousness or unconsciousness).

p97.original: 3. 预测最有可能的线索。仅仅“知道”某个材料并不意味着你看到考试题目时会自动将这一信息从长时记忆中带回意识。因此，花些时间来思考你的教授可能会提出的问题类型是值得的。例如，你将在本章中学习关于各种精神药物的作用，但如果教授要求你解释为什么酒精更像巴比妥类药物而非阿片类药物，你可能就会被难住了。通常，你可以通过注意教授在讲授中强调的内容来预测这些问题。考虑你的教授喜欢提出的问题类型也会有所帮助（有一个学习伙伴在这一方面会有很大帮助）。一些最常见的论述题会以“解释”“评价”或“比较和对比”等措辞开头。
p97.en: 3. Predicting the most likely clues. Just “knows” a material does not mean that you automatically bring this information back from the long-term memory when you see the subject of the examination. It would therefore be worthwhile to take some time to reflect on the type of questions your professor might raise. For example, in this chapter you will learn about the role of psychotropic substances, but if the professor asks you to explain why alcohol is more like barbiturates than opioids, you may be in danger. Usually, you can predict these problems by paying attention to what the professor has emphasized in his lectures. It would also be helpful to consider the type of questions your professor likes (a learning partner would be very helpful in this regard). Some of the most common topics for discussion begin with the words “explain” or “comparison and comparison”.

p98.original: 总之，意识和记忆之间的关系表明，要学习大学课程所要求的材料，你必须在这一材料还在你的意识之中时积极地加工它。要做到这一点，你必须使这一材料具有意义。这需要用你自己的话和例子来理解它，从而在新信息和你记忆中已有的旧信息之间建立联系。此外，你还需要组织信息，以便自己了解它们是如何相互联系的，并预测可以把这一材料带回到意识的线索。你越多地练习这些记忆策略，这一材料就能越快地在下一次考试中进入你的意识。
p98.en: In short, the relationship between consciousness and memory suggests that, in order to study the material required for university courses, you must actively process it while it is still in your mind. To do that, you must make this material meaningful. This requires understanding it with your own words and examples, thus linking new information with old information that is already in your memory. In addition, you need to organize information so that you can understand how they are connected and predict the clues that can be brought back to consciousness. The more you practice these memory strategies, the faster this material gets into your mind at the next exam.
